subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Microwaves: Heat and Data
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Microwaves: Heat and Data.

hook.text: A radar engineer noticed a candy bar melting in his pocket near a magnetron. Microwaves.

buildup.text: Microwaves oscillate water molecules. The friction heats food from the inside.

discovery.text: Microwave ovens use 2.45 GHz — a frequency water absorbs efficiently.

twist.text: Cell towers, Wi-Fi, and satellite links all transmit data on microwave frequencies.

climax.text: 5G networks use millimeter waves — the highest microwave band — for blazing speed.

punchline.text: Microwaves cook your food and carry your data — same physics, different use.

quiz.question: How do microwaves heat food?
options: They heat the air inside the oven, which cooks the food
They oscillate water molecules, generating friction and heat
They emit infrared radiation that penetrates the food surface
